Before we conduct our own testing on this SSD, Let’s take a closer look at the reported specifications and benchmarks first. The Sabrent Rocket PCIe 4.0 SSD arrives in multiple capacities (below). There are clear throughput improvements as you rise through the capacity tiers (not unusual), as does the rated 4K IOPS. Though one area worth focusing on a little is that TBW (terabytes Written) and DWPD (Drive writes per day), as this drive is THREE TIMES HIGHER than the Samsung 980 Pro and WD Black SN850 in terms of NAND lifespan on daily writes, likely down to that Kioxia 96 Layer 3D TLC NAND used, rather than the used by those used by competitors. This is an important point because the brand has significantly less pedigree in-home/business SSD media than the likes of Samsung, WD and Seagate and people will want to know they are going to get a product that lasts!

Title: Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB PCIe Gen4 M.2 NVMe SSD Review
URL: https://www.servethehome.com/sabrent-rocket-q4-2tb-pcie-gen4-m-2-nvme-ssd-review/
Published: 2020-12-26T20:10:32.000Z
Author: Will Taillac
Highlights:
## Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB

The Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB comes in a double-sided M.2 2280 (80mm) form factor.

Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB Front

Much like previous Sabrent drives, the drive label is applied on top of a thin copper heat spreader. Beneath the label and heatspreader there is the Phison PS5016-E16 controller, a DRAM cache, and 2 Micron 96L 512GB NAND packages.

Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB Back

The back has a product information label, the other half of the DRAM cache, and the other 2 512GB NAND packages. That brings the total NAND on the drive to 2048GB, which leaves 48GB reserved by the controller. This configuration is very common on consumer 2TB SSDs.

## Sabrent Rocket Q4 Specs

The Sabrent Rocket Q4 line of TLC-based SSDs has been announced in sizes ranging from 1TB to 4TB.

Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB Specs

Our 2TB drive is the middle SKU, and the specs are very close to the top end unit. This drive is rated at 4850 MB/s sequential read, and 3600 MB/s sequential write speeds. 400 TBW represents a smaller than average rated endurance for a drive of this size, and in fact all of the endurance levels for the Rocket Q4 line are on the small side. By comparison, the PCIe 3.0 Sabrent Rocket Q 2TB had a 530 TBW endurance rating, and the recently reviewed Sabrent Rocket 4 Plus 2TB with its TLC NAND had a rated endurance of 1400 TBW. While 400 TBW of endurance is still more than sufficient to last well beyond the warranty period for normal consumer loads, the overall downward trend of drive endurance is not a positive one and something we hope to see reverse course in time.

Sabrent Rocket Q4 2TB CrystalDiskInfo

CrystalDiskInfo can give us some basic information about the SSD, and confirms we are operating at PCIe 4.0 x4 speeds using NVMe 1.3.

Title: Sabrent Rocket Q4 2 TB Review | TechPowerUp
URL: https://www.techpowerup.com/review/sabrent-rocket-q4-2-tb/
Published: 2021-07-09T20:12:00.000Z
Author: W1zzard , on
Highlights:
Today, we have for review the Sabrent Rocket Q4, which, as the name suggests, uses the PCI-Express 4.0 interface, which doubles the theoretical bandwidth over PCI-Express Gen 3. Under the hood, the Sabrent Rocket Q4 uses a Phison E16 controller, which we've seen on drives like the Gigabyte PCIe 4.0 SSD, Seagate FireCuda 520, and Corsair MP600 Core. The former drives were all based on TLC NAND flash, but the Rocket Q4 uses QLC flash instead. The flash chips are Micron 96-layer QLC, pretty much the market-dominating QLC available at this time. Two DDR4-2666 DRAM chips provide 2 GB of memory for the mapping tables of the SSD. The Sabrent Rocket Q4 comes in capacities of 1 TB ($150), 2 TB ($300), and 4 TB ($700). Endurance for these models is set to 200 TBW, 400 TBW, and 800 TBW respectively. Sabrent includes a five-year warranty with the Rocket Q4. The big heatsink adds $20 to the price point.

## FAQ

Is this drive compatible with my system?

You must have a motherboard with an available M.2 socket that supports a NVMe drive. It may be possible to use an enclosure or adapter, but NVMe boot support on older systems is not guaranteed. This drive is backward compatible with PCIe 3.0 and 2.0 even with fewer than four lanes, but will be bandwidth-limited.

What is the warranty for this drive?

1 year or 5 years with registration. Endurance is rated at 400TBW for the 2TB SKU.

What's the hardware on the SSD?

This drive utilizes Phison's E16 controller with DRAM, along with 96-layer or newer QLC.
